To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ClpB Hsp100 N-terminal domains (NTD) play an important regulatory role in protein aggregation by binding to the substrate and destabilizing the protein, priming it for subsequent unfolding and aggregation.

the ClpB Hsp100 chaperone recognizes exposed hydrophobics stretches in unfolded or misfolded proteins via a substrate binding groove located in its NTD, and that the NTD also plays a regulatory role by blocking the translocation pore and destabilizing client protein prior to their disaggregation.
the ClpB Hsp100 N-terminal domains (NTDs) bind to exposed hydrophobic regions in aggregated proteins and have a regulatory role in ClpB-mediated protein disaggregation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of protein quality control in cells.
how proteins can be unfolded, refolded, and reactivated by the chaperone machinery.
the structure and function of ClpB, an AAA+ (ATPase associated with various cellular activities) protein that is involved in protein disaggregation and refolding in bacteria, yeast and plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ClpB N-Terminal domain is a regulatory domain that plays a role in substrate binding and protein disaggregation.
ClpB N-Terminal Domain is a key regulator in the process of protein disaggregation.
the N-terminal domains of the Clp/Hsp100 disaggregase are important for the recognition of unfolded and misfolded proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NTD of ClpB has a regulatory role in disaggregation, which includes blocking the translocation pore in the absence of substrates, and destabilizing client protein aggregates upon binding, thus promoting their unfolding and translocation.
the NTD is a regulatory element that controls ClpB function in protein disaggregation and that the NTD plays a role in both client protein binding and protein translocation.
the NTD of ClpB is a key regulatory component of the disaggregation cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, besides the pore-loop tyrosl residues, ClpB/HSP100 has an N-terminal domain that is essential for the recognition and translocation of substrates.
the ClpB–client interaction is mediated by two distinct sites, the N-terminal substrate-binding groove and the central pore–located pore-loop tyrosine residues.
the NTD is not only involved in substrate recognition but also plays a regulatory role that includes destabilizing client proteins and blocking the central translocation channel.
